summary.headline: Exicom Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 46% YoY to INR 388 crores and consolidated EBITDA turned positive at INR 0.3 crore for the first time since Tritium acquisition.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 revenue grew 33% YoY to INR 282 crores with EBITDA of INR 29.9 crores (10.6% margin), driven by Critical Power (+23% YoY) and EVSE (+60% YoY). Consolidated revenue of INR 388 crores (+46% YoY) included Tritium, and consolidated EBITDA turned marginally positive. For full FY26, consolidated EBITDA was still negative at INR 103 crores and adjusted PAT was negative at INR 258 crores, with higher finance cost and one-time exceptional costs (VRS, Tritium retention, labour code). Management flagged a temporary inventory and receivables build as Hyderabad ramped up alongside Gurgaon.

financial_highlights.change: hit by finance cost, exceptional items, labour code

segments.name: Critical Power (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 194 crores (consolidated ~INR 198 crores), up 23% YoY and ~18% QoQ; order book about INR 1,000 crores at 31 March. Exports hit a record ~INR 30 crores in Q4 (~15% of Critical Power sales vs ~10% historically).

segments.name: EVSE / EV charging (standalone)
segments.commentary: Grew 60% YoY in Q4 and 40% for FY26; record quarterly EV charging revenue of INR 88 crores (management figure, basis not specified). Full-year EVSE consolidated growth 72%; Q4 consolidated EVSE +83% YoY.

segments.name: Tritium (US/Australia, EV charging)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about $10 million (sales $9.7 million), record order intake $10 million; EBITDA losses down about 30% QoQ. Management targets ~3x revenue and 25% lower EBITDA losses, with EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Tritium: revenue to scale about 3x and EBITDA losses to fall about 25%; EBITDA breakeven targeted in Q4 FY27. Management said losses fall less sharply than revenue because low-cost acquired inventory is being used up, with margins normalising after about one quarter.
Exports: target to lift Critical Power export share to 20% in FY27 from ~10-15%.
Non-telecom BESS: internal target of over INR 50 crores business in FY26 from pilot-stage orders; management sees BESS possibly reaching ~30% of Critical Power over 2-3 years if successful.

Three Tritium products (TRI-FLEX inverter and two others) launching May-July 2026; management cites about INR 850 crores of combined FY28 revenue potential, subject to pilots. TRI-FLEX hyperscaler factory acceptance test ongoing, potentially $30-35 million FY28 revenue.
Gurgaon production to shift majority to Hyderabad over the next 2-3 months; inventory build expected to normalise over coming quarters.

Additional open opportunities of about INR 400 crores beyond the INR 1,000 crore Critical Power order book, including about INR 100 crores of new BharatNet tenders and about INR 150 crores of uncovered-village Phase-2.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant (newly inaugurated early March 2026) became fully operational in Q4 FY26 after Q3 trials; added depreciation is reflected in Q4 numbers.
Gurgaon plant still running; majority of production to move to Hyderabad over the next 2-3 months, with some production retained in Gurgaon.
Tritium manufacturing in Tennessee, US; R&D in Brisbane, Australia; Exicom R&D in Gurgaon (hardware) and Bangalore (software), with 130+ engineers.
Ring-topology PC charger: first pilot in Q4 FY26, mass production planned in FY27.
Exicom One: 80 sites executed in Q4 under this integrated products-and-services program.
demand_pricing: Critical Power pricing on BharatNet and other government contracts is fixed, so Q4 contribution margin was slightly below Q3 due to input cost increases from forex, commodities and geopolitical factors.
Management said large high-volume orders (e.g. a DC power system order above INR 100 crores with a leading Indian telco) help offset input cost inflation.
Standalone gross margin expanded to 27% on richer EVSE mix and fewer low-margin lithium battery sales.
EV demand: FY26 described as a record year with monthly EV sales above 200,000 across categories; electric car penetration cited as 5% and three-wheeler penetration 32%.

Competition noted in BESS and the market was described as large and competitive; BESS cell supply is import-dependent (China) until local cell manufacturing arrives, expected next year or the year after.

qa_highlights.question: What charging infrastructure is needed for commercial EV adoption and where is it happening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adoption is in fixed-route captive use such as ports, cement distribution and mining with 200-300 trucks; intercity commercial electrification is still about two years away.

qa_highlights.question: What is the product and revenue potential of the TRI-FLEX inverter and its applications?
qa_highlights.answer: TRI-FLEX converts grid power to high-voltage DC for DC microgrids, BESS integration and 800V data centres. A hyperscaler pilot is in testing and, if successful, could unlock significant FY28 revenue ($30-35 million cited).

qa_highlights.question: How will the company win customers for the two other new Tritium products in the US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said development was done with existing strategic customers, and it has line of sight to long-term contracts once pilots succeed.

qa_highlights.question: Does Exicom have OEM tie-ups for supplying chargers with vehicles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Exicom is the largest home charger maker, with about a 50% chance a new EV in India comes with an Exicom charger, and it has OEM partnerships for home and fast chargers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS offering and its scaling path over 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets commercial and industrial modular BESS, not utility, transmission, distribution or home. About 10-20 small projects were deployed in Q4, with an FY26 target above INR 50 crores, and BESS could reach about 30% of Critical Power over 2-3 years.

risks_watch: Consolidated FY26 EBITDA -INR 103 crores and adjusted PAT -INR 258 crores; breakeven depends on Tritium reaching 3x revenue and EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27.
Tritium margin normalisation as low-cost acquired inventory is consumed after about one quarter.
Working capital: inventory build from parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad operations and higher receivables; collections and normalisation to be tracked.
Input cost inflation (forex, commodities, geopolitics) against fixed-price government BharatNet contracts.
Telecom tower installations slipped slightly in Q4; Critical Power demand depends on telco capex.
New Tritium products depend on hyperscaler pilot success and multi-month launch timelines (May-July 2026).
BESS cell supply dependent on imports until local cell manufacturing arrives.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, EVSE momentum and Tritium turnaround, while cautious on near-term Tritium margins, working capital and geopolitical or supply-chain headwinds. The CFO was less specific on the reasons for the full-year PAT loss and on receivables quality.
key_quotes: This reflects better product mix, sharper execution and Tritium beginning to scale commercially.
But we are firmly on our path for EBITDA breakeven at Tritium in Quarter 4 of FY '27 and the 3x revenue growth paved the way for it.
This is by design. We are stocking up both facilities to ensure smooth production continuity during this transition and to support an order book we are seeing in FY'27.

adds.what: Hyderabad plant (inaugurated early March 2026), fully operational in Q4 FY26

growth.why: Management guides Tritium revenue to scale about 3x in FY27 with EBITDA losses down about 25% and breakeven in Q4 FY27, backed by a INR 1,000 crore Critical Power order book, record Tritium order intake of $10 million, and the Hyderabad plant now fully running; no explicit consolidated revenue growth figure was given.
